transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Time: 18:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (CEO), Aiden Park (CTO), Ravi Singh (VP Eng), Sofia Martinez (Head of Product), Elena Brooks (CFO), Noah Patel (Head of Sales), Grace Liu (Dir DevRel) + company-wide attendees

Summary:
- Year-end review: business metrics, hiring pause and headcount plan, product/infrastructure wins (Dedicated scaling, caching improvements).
- Roadmap highlights for Q1: reliability and Private product push, cost/perf initiatives, SOC2 progress and enterprise readiness.
- Operational notes: holiday on-call, freeze windows, customer communications.

Topics:
- Business performance and ARR cadence
- Product wins: Dedicated, Redwood Console improvements, Optimize tooling
- Security & compliance: SOC2 timeline, KMS/HSM work, audit readiness
- Hiring and budget posture
- Customer success highlights and top accounts

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey, uh, thanks everyone for joining - appreciate you carving time this, uh, right before the holidays. We'll keep it tight, but want to run through Q4 numbers, big ops things, and what to expect in Q1.

[00:22] Elena Brooks: Quick note on slides: Q4 came in slightly ahead of plan, revenue growth at 38% YoY, ARR expansion driven by Dedicated deals, and renewals looking strong. Burn is down versus forecast, we're in good shape but we'll be disciplined on hires early Q1.

[00:45] Noah Patel: Sales had a few enterprise pushes in EMEA and one major deal that moved from POC to committed in December - team did a great job. We did see more security diligence from prospects asking for SOC2 evidence and private deploy options, that slowed some closures.

[01:12] Maya Chen: Right, the ask for SOC2 and Private is consistent with our thesis - customers want serving control. Aiden, quick update on SOC2 and infra?

[01:25] Aiden Park: Sure. We're about 70% through the controls work, auditors in Jan for the readiness review. KMS integration for Private and Dedicated is in staging; HSM proof-of-concept completed with partner, um, vendor name in notes, small transcription glitch, it's all good. On the runtime side we've landed the KV cache improvements which reduced tail latency for chat workloads by, um, median 12-18% in our internal bench. Some noise in the benchmarks where the seq length distribution caused kernel fallback, we'll fine tune in Q1.

[02:03] Ravi Singh: To add, continuous batching and the new kernel selection heuristics cut cost-per-token on average for the 8k context models. We're also locking a minimal set of quantization profiles to reduce variability for Dedicated customers. There were a couple of incidents this month around autoscaler thrash when a client burst happened; we've mitigations queued.

[02:40] Sofia Martinez: From Product: Redwood Console updates shipped - better per-route cost breakdowns, token-level charts, and rollout controls. We're prioritizing the Private UX next quarter; customers keep asking for clearer rollout metrics and RBAC on the private plane, SSO improvements too.

[03:05] Grace Liu: On developer community side, the adoption of our quickstart and benchmark repo grew 30% - folks are using the sample harness for latency/cost comparisons. We posted a benchmark note but had a small naming issue where some community posts referenced 'Redwood Serve' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated' - minor but we'll correct.

[03:35] Maya Chen: Nice. A couple of questions from the chat about pricing and dedicated vs hosted - can we give a quick frame?

[03:45] Noah Patel: Short: hosted is fastest to start, reserved Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit economics at scale, Private for regulated customers who need VPC/hardware isolation. We showed a slide earlier with crossover points - basically at sustained heavy throughput, Dedicated reduces per-token cost by significant margin.

[04:06] Attendee (Q): How about on-prem options and support SLAs?

[04:12] Aiden Park: We're shipping Private deployments that can be air-gapped for on-prem; we've got a few pilot customers. SLA tiers for Private are part of our enterprise contracts with optional managed support. There was a small misspelling in the doc earlier - said 'airgapped' without hyphen, you know, transcription wants the nit picky stuff.

[04:36] Elena Brooks: Finance note: we plan a modest hiring pause for Jan to evaluate Q1 priorities. Critical hires for infra and security will continue. Expect headcount guidance from People early next week.

[05:02] Maya Chen: OK, on operational side - holiday on-call and freeze window? Ravi?

[05:12] Ravi Singh: Freeze window starts 2026-12-24 through 2026-12-27 for non-critical changes. We'll have a reduced on-call roster, details posted in the runbook. Critical security patches still go out but with ECC review. Also, please don't schedule large deploys during that window.

[05:36] Sofia Martinez: Product roadmap for Q1: 1) Private UX + RBAC, 2) Reliability SLOs and better autoscaler behaviors, 3) Release Redwood Optimize features for batching suggestions and quantization recommendations, 4) Expand model catalog with vetted open models for latency/cost tradeoffs.

[06:05] Maya Chen: Thank you. A couple of calls out - top customers we won in Q4, and some churn reasons: pricing sensitivity and internal procurement timelines. We should get security docs into the sales pack.

[06:24] Noah Patel: Agreed - I'll coordinate with Aiden on a concise security one-pager we can share. Also we need an updated pricing appendix for Dedicated runs.

[06:43] Aiden Park: We'll produce a SOC2 progress note and a KMS/HSM summary. Also, some technical deep-dive offers: we'll offer a performance benchmark for any large account to prove latency/cost on their workloads. That helps unblock procurement.

[07:05] Attendee (Engineering): Quick question about KV cache invalidation and customer-specific caches - any changes?

[07:12] Ravi Singh: We're pushing a safer default invalidation window and adding per-tenant cache metrics to Console so customers can see hit rates. That should help debugging and cost understanding.

[07:34] Grace Liu: On the community & marketing side - holiday content schedule: share year-in-review highlights, a blog about benchmarking best practices, and a shorter note on our Dedicated case study.

[07:54] Maya Chen: OK let's run through a short Q&A and then close with thanks.

[08:03] Attendee (Sales): Are we changing discounts for enterprise in Q1?

[08:10] Elena Brooks: We'll keep disciplined on net-new discounts; we'll allow structured credits for committed Dedicated seats instead of across-the-board percent discounts. Fiscal discipline is important.

[08:30] Attendee (Product): Any change to support SLAs for Dedicated customers?

[08:36] Sofia Martinez: No change to SLAs right now; instead we're offering faster response tiers as an add-on. We will formalize the tiers in the Service Addendum next quarter.

[08:50] Maya Chen: Final wrap - big thanks to everyone, remarkable work on infra and sales in Q4, let's keep the momentum. Enjoy the break, be safe, and we'll reconvene Jan for the Q1 kickoff.

[09:05] Maya Chen: Quick housekeeping: action items on slides, Elena will post P&L, Ravi will publish freeze & on-call, Aiden will send SOC2 note, Sofia will set the Q1 roadmap meeting.

[09:25] Maya Chen: Happy holidays, folks!
